nodes.name: PSCF Sol-gel Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.2 mmol of Pr(NO3)3·6H2O, 1.8 mmol of Sr(NO3)2, 1 mmol of Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 1 mmol of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O and 4 mmol of CA were dissolved in 30 ml of H2O. Then, 4 mmol of EDTA was slowly added. Finally, the NH3·H2O was dropwise added to adjust the pH value to 7–8. The beaker containing the solution was then placed on a heating platform at 90°C with continuously stirring until a gel was formed. The beaker was then transferred to an oven at 200°C for 10 h. After that, the obtained precursor was taken out, thoroughly ground, and then pre-calcined in a muffle furnace at 400°C for 2 h. Subsequently, the sample was heated to 850°C at a heating rate of 5°C min^-1 and maintained at 850°C for 6 h in air to obtain PSCF powder.

nodes.name: PSCFM Sol-gel Synthesis
nodes.procedure: For the synthesis of PSCFM, the stoichiometric amount of C4H6MnO4 was used as a precursor to replace the stoichiometric amount of Fe in the PSCF synthesis recipe. [Follows identical procedure as PSCF: 0.2 mmol Pr(NO3)3·6H2O, 1.8 mmol Sr(NO3)2, 1 mmol Co(NO3)2·6H2O, reduced Fe(NO3)3·9H2O + stoichiometric C4H6MnO4, 4 mmol CA, 4 mmol EDTA in 30 ml H2O, pH 7-8 with NH3·H2O, gelation at 90°C, drying at 200°C for 10h, grinding, pre-calcination at 400°C for 2h, final calcination at 850°C for 6h in air].

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms average particle size of ~100 nm for PSCFM with uniform elemental dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image confirms the average particle size of ~100 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and elemental maps confirm uniform dispersion of all elements without phase segregation in PSCFM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic-scale high-angle annular dark field (HAADF)-scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and elemental maps (Fig. 3b) confirm the uniform dispersion of all elements without observable phase segregation.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals oxidative valence states: Co 2.46/2.49, Fe 2.38/2.37, Mn 3.39 for PSCFM/PSCF; O 1s shows higher P2+P3 (79.6%) in PSCFM indicating more oxygen vacancy-related species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Subsequent X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) characterization revealed the oxidative valence states of each cation in PSCF... the XPS analysis revealed an estimated chemical valence of Co is 2.46 and 2.49 for PSCFM and PSCF, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co L-edge and Fe L3-edge XAS confirm similar Co (2+/3+) and Fe valence states in PSCF and PSCFM; O K-edge shows enhanced metal 3d-O 2p hybridization in PSCFM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This near-identical chemical valence is confirmed by the Co L-edge XAS... The overlapping Co L3-edge peak positions of PSCF and PSCFM further indicate their similar Co valence states.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) measured by CV at non-faradaic potentials; PSCF Cdl = 2.15 mF cm^-2 (MOR), PSCFM Cdl = 2.66 mF cm^-2 (MOR), similar ECSA values for all catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) and electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) were both measured and calculated (Fig. 3d, Supplementary Fig. 14 and Supplementary Table 7). The Cdl for PSCF (2.15 mF cm^-2) and PSCFM (2.66 mF cm^-2) in MOR are similar to those achieved in OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ EIS shows PSCFM has lower Rct at all potentials and highest frequency of 9.8 Hz indicating fastest OH- adsorption kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, in situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was conducted at different potentials... The PSCFM with a lower Rct at all potentials exhibits faster kinetics in the adsorption of OH- during OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows higher Co dissolution in PSCF (7.59 ppb) vs PSCFM (4.01 ppb) after stability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ICP-MS measurement highlights the higher loss of Co in PSCF (7.59 ppb) compared to PSCFM (4.01 ppb).
